title: Can Concrete Existential-Safety Criteria Be Met? A Document Audit Pilot

original_idea.body:
# Can Concrete Existential-Safety Criteria Be Met? A Document Audit Pilot

**Problem:** The FLI AI Safety Index 2025 found no company scored above D in existential safety planning. The suggested follow-up is to develop concrete criteria for higher scores and test whether any company could meet them — but the criteria do not yet exist in checkable form.

**Direction:** Operationalize 5-8 binary, evidence-checkable criteria for existential-safety planning (e.g. published capability thresholds, third-party eval commitments, pause conditions). Use an LLM with a strict rubric to extract evidence from public safety frameworks/system cards of 3-4 labs, then hand-verify. Report which criteria are met and inter-rater agreement between the LLM and human.

**Why it matters:** Turns a vague D-grade into a transparent, reproducible scorecard outsiders can maintain, pressuring labs with concrete gaps. Document analysis only — zero compute, maximally lab-independent.

**Relevant context:** FLI AI Safety Index 2025: no company scored above D in existential safety planning; subfield note suggests developing concrete criteria for higher scores and testing attainability.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a checkable existential-safety scorecard pressures labs on a pathway major safety orgs flag.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Document analysis + LLM rubric extraction + hand-verify; accessible, no GPU needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused scorecard pilot but operationalizing criteria + multi-lab extraction spans workstreams.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Pure governance document audit, maximally lab-independent, outsider scrutiny labs won't self-do; neglected gold.

novelty.reasoning: Operationalizing existential-safety criteria into a checkable scorecard appears mostly novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Turning the FLI D-grade into concrete checkable criteria appears mostly novel.
